reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G3-NA-Q4-Harden (mat_g3_na_q4_6), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The items directly assess representing fractions equal to one (e.g., "A shape is divided into 8 equal parts. 8 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?" yielding 8/8) and fractions greater than one (e.g., "A shape is divided into 3 equal parts. 5 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?" yielding 5/3). The core concept of equal partitioning and unit fraction counting beyond one whole is solidly demonstrated.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set comprehensively covers fractions equal to one (such as "A shape is divided into 5 equal parts. 5 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?" and "A shape is divided into 6 equal parts with 6 parts shaded. The fraction shaded is ___.") as well as fractions greater than one across varied unit sizes (e.g., "A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?" and "A shape is divided into 5 equal parts. 9 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reading level and syntactic complexity are well-calibrated for Grade 3 Quarter 4 students. Prompts like "A shape is divided into 3 equal parts with 10 parts shaded. The fraction shaded is ___." are succinct and unambiguous, ensuring that students are tested on their fractional reasoning rather than deciphering complex sentence structures.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The items feature diverse question formats including multiple-choice questions (e.g., "A shape is divided into 6 equal parts. 11 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?") and fill-in-the-blank / cloze questions (e.g., "A shape is divided into 6 equal parts with 14 parts shaded. The fraction shaded is ___."), covering simple improper fractions, whole-number multiples like "A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 8 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?", and unitary whole fractions.

competency_alignment.rationale: The problem set maintains strict alignment with MATATAG learning competency mat_g3_na_q4_6. It avoids out-of-scope mixed numbers, operations, or abstract fraction equations, staying firmly focused on model-based fraction identification such as "A shape is divided into 3 equal parts. 8 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?".

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The denominators used (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8) reflect standard Grade 3 fraction modeling bounds, and the numerator values (e.g., in "A shape is divided into 8 equal parts. 18 parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?") are reasonable for multi-shape visual representation models at this grade level.
